glosses: to neigh, to whinny, to nicker (sound of a horse)

examples.text: Detlef kann ausgezeichnet Tierstimmen imitieren: Er gackert wie ein Huhn, schnattert wie eine Ente, wiehert wie ein Pferd oder bellt wie ein Hund.
examples.translation: Detlef sait imiter les voix d’animaux excellemment : Il caquette comme une poule, nasille comme un canard, hennit comme un cheval ou aboie comme un chien.

examples.text: Auf Wiesen kann man Pferde wiehern hören.
Die Kinder wieherten vor Vergnügen.

And moving out they found the stately horse, / Who now no more a vassal to the thief, / But free to stretch his limbs in lawful fight, / Neigh'd with all gladness as they came, and stoop'd / With a low whinny toward the pair: […]
Cattle lowed here and there, and horses whinnied to be fed.
A pony whinnied a short distance from the hut.
[John Gray] whinnies like a donnish Houyhnhnm[.]

glosses: To emit a snicker, a stifled or broken laugh.

examples.text: I have seen the eternal Footman hold my coat, and snicker, / And in short, I was afraid.

glosses: To utter through a laugh of this kind.
A player who snicks the ball.

examples.text: This coat cost me 50 nicker.
Seems? Well, this seems to be a waste of my time. That is 900 nicker in any shop you're lucky enough to find one in. And you're complaining about 200? What school of finance did you study?

glosses: A soft neighing sound characteristic of a horse.
To make a soft neighing sound characteristic of a horse.

examples.text: Behind him, old Akthoob was grumbling loudly, saying something about the midday meal, and Haral, the black Feridoon pony, snuffing in the old, familiar scent of the green meadows of the Chaya's banks, the warm sweet smells of home, was nickering eagerly.

"Nasrullah's nickerin’, Mr. Arthur. Somethin's wrong."
"Hell, he's nickered before. He nickers all the time!"
Robinson and Snow looked at each other, saying nothing for a moment, and finally Snow told Hancock that Nasrullah never nickered in the paddock.
After a few minutes, the mare walked over and nickered loudly in his ear, and he immediately got to his feet and stripped the gear from the waiting horse.

glosses: To produce a snigger or suppressed laugh.
One of the night brawlers of London formerly noted for breaking windows with halfpence.

examples.text:

your modern musicians want art to defend their windows from common nickers

glosses: The cutting lip which projects downward at the edge of a boring bit and cuts a circular groove in the wood to limit the size of the hole that is bored.
Someone who nicks (steals) something, a thief.

examples.text: He […] was far more interested in the fact that I was a car thief and an expert driver than that I was a bandit. […] Car nicker, are you?

glosses: A type of mythological sea creature or sea monster; also, a water sprite; a nix or nixie; a mermaid or merman.

examples.text: And in another tale, told at Kemnitz of the Nicker, as he is there called, when he asks the midwife how much he owes her, she answers that she will take no more from him than from other people.
"I went into the stable first to see to the horse, and found him neighing and waiting for his hay, so I went up into the hay-loft for an armful[.]"

glosses: To make a sound similar to a horse's cry.

examples.text: Yes, yes, 'tis he. I will assure you Uncle, the very he, the he your Wisdom plaid withal, I thank you for't, neighed at his Nakedness, and made his Cold and Poverty your Pastime; […]

glosses: Faire entendre son cri ordinaire, en parlant du cheval ou du zèbre.

examples.text: J’aimais aussi alors, comme aujourd’hui, à voir les armes reluire au soleil, à entendre les chevaux hennir et frapper du pied, […].
En effet, au bout de cinq minutes de marche, le cheval releva la tête et hennit comme pour annoncer son arrivée, […].
Alors les chevaux, excités par les coups de fouets des chasseurs, se précipitèrent dans toutes les directions en hennissant et en lançant des ruades.

Tant qu'a duré ce défilé j'ai eu toutes les peines du monde à faire tenir mon cheval tranquille. Grisé par tout ce bruit et ce mouvement autour de nous, il hennit, piaffe, s’ébroue et danse d'impatience de se mêler à ses congénères.
Le Pourquoi pas, lutte, lutte toujours. Mais déjà les chevaux blancs des Walkyries hennissent dans les rafales.
